clue.text: Bridge opponents demand order for coffee

parts.note: in bridge East and South sit as opponents, giving E and S
the second of the pair, South, gives S
to press is to demand insistently
O stands for Order, as in OBE

explanation.surface: Someone at the card table wants a strong coffee brought over.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is a strong Italian coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: The Spanish nonetheless produce a cricket team

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine article
even so, still, nevertheless

explanation.surface: Despite everything, Spain manages to field a side for a cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket side has this many players, so the number names the team.

clue.text: Aristocrat keeps riding with favourite entertainer

indicators.note: the aristocrat holds the other pieces within him

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility
up means on horseback, riding
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A noble keeps a favourite performer around while out on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who works marionettes or glove figures is a kind of entertainer.

clue.text: Throw out 6 in 13

indicators.note: the number six sits inside the therapy abbreviation

parts.note: points to 13-across, a word for therapy; ECT is electroconvulsive therapy
six in Roman numerals is VI

explanation.surface: A cross-referencing instruction to throw something out.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 6 is read as a plain number, not as the 6-down answer, and 13 stands for the 13-across word, of which ECT is one form.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict a tenant is to throw them out of a property legally.

clue.text: Old Bob's inclined to be pompous

parts.note: a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated s
tilted means leaning, inclined

explanation.surface: An elderly man named Bob tends towards self-importance.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob was British slang for a shilling, the pre-1971 coin written s.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilted speech is stiff and unnatural, much like pompous or formal language.

clue.text: This eavesdropper will run away if the situation hots up

definitions.text: This eavesdropper will run away if the situation hots up

parts.words: This eavesdropper will run away if the situation hots up
parts.note: an eavesdropper here hangs drip-like from the eaves, and running away is melting when it gets warmer

explanation.surface: A snoop who flees as soon as things get dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging spike of frozen water hangs from eaves and melts and runs off when warmed.

clue.text: One opposed to well-established painter

parts.note: a con is an argument against, as in pros and cons
stable means firmly established

explanation.surface: Someone resists a long-established artist.
explanation.definitionFit: John Constable was an English landscape artist, so he is an example of a painter.

clue.text: Half-heartedly set up in the Mediterranean

indicators.note: the two central letters form the heart, and half of that, one letter, is dropped

parts.note: to create is to set up or establish

explanation.surface: Something established without enthusiasm on a Mediterranean shore.
explanation.walkthrough: CREATE has EA at its heart; losing half of that, the A, leaves the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Crete is a large Greek island lying in the Mediterranean Sea.

clue.text: Let it end with development being authorised

indicators.note: development means the letters are built into a new form

explanation.surface: Let a story finish once it has been fully developed and approved.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entitled means having been given a right or authorisation.

clue.text: Former president's authorised to be outspoken

parts.note: ex means former
P is the standard abbreviation for president
licit means lawful, authorised

explanation.surface: An ex-president is allowed to speak his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicit statements are frank and direct, as an outspoken person is.

clue.text: Six-footer in religious faction

parts.note: a sect is a religious faction

explanation.surface: A very tall person belongs to a religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person, but it means a creature with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects have six legs, making them literal six-footers.

clue.text: Money from chapel funds

indicators.note: from shows the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Cash taken out of the chapel's coffers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelf is an old, disparaging word for money or riches.

clue.text: Work very hard for penniless authority

indicators.note: without a penny, and P is the abbreviation for penny

parts.note: an expert is an authority on a subject

explanation.surface: A broke specialist puts in a lot of effort.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert oneself is to make a great physical or mental effort.

clue.text: Action to help mate floundering in river

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit within the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a major English river

indicators.note: floundering means struggling clumsily, so the letters tumble around

explanation.surface: Someone tries to aid a friend who is struggling in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical care given to a patient is action intended to help them.

clue.text: Abhorred keeping Ethiopian leader angry

indicators.note: the first word holds the extra letter inside it

parts.note: abhorred means hated

indicators.note: a leader is the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Hated by people who are holding an Ethiopian ruler, and furious.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated exchange is an angry one, so heated is a synonym of angry.

clue.text: Unrest developed when keeping toilet free

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap round the toilet word
developed means made into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Trouble broke out when protesters took over a public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something loose is to set it free.

clue.text: Jeweller replaced bag free

indicators.note: replaced means put back in a different position, so the letters change places

explanation.surface: A bag of jewellery was replaced at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like it means 'at no cost', but it is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Carl Fabergé was a Russian jeweller famous for his jewelled eggs.

clue.text: Strengthen and control troops

parts.note: to rein in is to control
a force is a body of troops

explanation.surface: Supporting a position by bringing up soldiers and keeping them disciplined.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce a structure or army is to strengthen it.

clue.text: Evangelists in employment? Drinks all round!

indicators.note: the drinks surround the work word

parts.note: ales are beers, drinks
a post is a job, employment

explanation.surface: Missionaries at work are offered a round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles spread the Christian gospel, making them evangelists in the broad sense.

clue.text: Present wine with fish

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Serving wine alongside a fish dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray someone is to depict or present them in a work.

clue.text: Cart turned up in enclosure

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a dray is a heavy brewer's cart

explanation.surface: A cart was found upended in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard is an enclosed area, as in a farmyard or courtyard.

clue.text: Believe in direct production

indicators.note: production means the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: Having faith in a film director's work.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit a story is to believe it.

clue.text: Sign of cold makes sailor stay in car that's hot

indicators.note: the sailor remains inside the car

parts.note: taken as written
a tar is a sailor
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A seaman with a chill stays inside his warm car.
explanation.definitionFit: Catarrh is excess mucus in the nose and throat, a symptom of a cold.

clue.text: Frequently visits hotel with relatives

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
aunts are relatives

explanation.surface: Someone often stays at a hotel with family.
explanation.definitionFit: To haunt a place is to go there often, as a regular does.

clue.text: Become suspicious when Pasternak heroine tucks into fish

indicators.note: the heroine goes inside the fish

parts.note: the smelt is a small silvery fish
Lara is the heroine of Boris Pasternak's Doctor Zhivago

explanation.surface: A Russian novel's heroine eating fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom to smell a rat means to suspect something is wrong.

clue.text: The 18 creator upset student in frenzy

indicators.note: the student goes inside the reversed word
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: rage is a frenzy
L is a learner driver, a student

explanation.surface: The composer of an oratorio flies into a frenzy over a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 is the 18-down answer, an oratorio of 1903 by this English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar composed the oratorio The Apostles, so he is its creator.

clue.text: One sinks into seat? That's capital!

indicators.note: the one goes inside the seat

parts.note: a sofa is a seat
one is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone collapses onto a couch and calls it excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's capital!' sounds like praise, but capital is the definition: a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Pole fighting man in crowd

parts.note: S is the South Pole
war is fighting
M is the abbreviation for male, man

explanation.surface: A Polish soldier in the middle of a throng.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large crowd, as of insects or people.

clue.text: The French behave in the water

parts.note: la is the French feminine article
to go on is to behave, as in the way someone goes on

explanation.surface: French people misbehaving in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A lagoon is a stretch of shallow water cut off from the sea.

clue.text: Turn liar out of rehearsal

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Deciding to stop lying during a practice session.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run is a test performance, a rehearsal before the real thing.

clue.text: Mortar used for levelling a long passage

definitions.meaning: a smooth layer of cement laid on a floor
a lengthy, often tedious, piece of writing

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a flooring layer of mortar and a long tedious piece of writing.

clue.text: Cleaners accepting decoration in judge's room

indicators.note: the cleaners take the decoration inside

parts.note: chars are charwomen, cleaners
an MBE is an honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: Office cleaners receive an honour in a judge's office.
explanation.walkthrough: A char, or charwoman, is a British word for a domestic cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's chambers are their private rooms in court.
